blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Eagle Ridge. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Eagle Ridge, Coquitlam: 10 condos and townhomes listed at the end of October 2026 and 3 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 30%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. By listings that is number 10 of 23 Coquitlam communities for condos and townhomes.

Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: The western anchor is in the next municipality: Eagle Ridge Hospital is at 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, at the area's west side, on Fraser Health's own location page.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Eagle Ridge Court at 1170 Lansdowne Drive is the area's documented strata conversion: City of Coquitlam Subdivision Committee minutes of July 3, 1980 record a strata title conversion application for 1170 Lansdowne Street by Cressey Development Corporation, with an undertaking that existing tenants would not be ejected to ease sale of the units, and a recommendation to waive the conversion guideline vacancy factor of 3.5%.

The second complex is the 16-unit townhouse project at 1135 Lansdowne Drive, recorded under construction in City Design Committee minutes of September 27, 1988, which reviewed revised colours for that project.

The rest of the Lansdowne corridor at this end is detached houses and the Eagle Ridge Park school campus, so Eagle Ridge attached choice is effectively a choice between these named complexes, not a long building list.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The conversion history is the rule that shapes diligence at 1170 Lansdowne Drive: because the complex began as rental housing and was converted to strata under the 1980 application, its strata documents and building systems history read differently from a purpose-built strata of the same era.

Creek and slope checks apply on the corridor's greenbelt edges under the City's Schedule B Environmental Development Permit Areas map, which maps watercourse, unstable-slope and Interface Wildfire Risk Management layers — the map shows layers, not a lot-level conclusion.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Eagle Ridge Park, entrance at 2635 Runnel Drive and fronting Lansdowne Drive at the schools, holds natural grass soccer and rugby fields, baseball and softball diamonds, a lacrosse box with four pickleball courts, four lit tennis courts, a playground, trails and washrooms — the recreation base directly in front of the Lansdowne complexes.

Eagle Ridge Outdoor Pool is a subfacility of that park: an eight-lane, 25-metre outdoor pool with 1-metre and 3-metre diving boards, with a listed 2026 season of May 30 to September 7 — seasonal, not year-round.

The Coquitlam Crunch Trail starts at Eagle Ridge Park and climbs 2.2 kilometres with 894 steps and 242 metres of elevation gain to Westwood Plateau, so the Lansdowne townhouses sit at the trail's bottom access point.

Scott Creek's drainage work touches this corridor directly: the City's instream-works list names Scott Creek at Lansdowne Drive and Scott Creek at Eagleridge Drive as box-culvert clean-and-inspect sites.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: No municipal page states strata fees or contingency amounts for Eagle Ridge Court or 1135 Lansdowne Drive, so those come only from the unit's Form B and strata documents.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the conversion-era building systems at 1170 Lansdowne Drive first: the 1980 conversion minutes are the starting document, and the strata's depreciation report is where envelope, roof and plumbing history for that complex is actually stated.

Check creek proximity on the City's creeks and environmental mapping for units near the Scott Creek corridor, which the City classifies for environmental value and monitors for flow, level and water quality.
Check slope and wildfire-interface layers on Schedule B Environmental Development Permit Areas before assuming a greenbelt-edge unit at 1135 Lansdowne Drive carries no permit overlay.

blocks.text: Eagle Ridge home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

14 townhomes sold in Eagle Ridge with a median price of $873,250 (the middle half sold between $838,750 and $1,029,250), taking a median of 16 days to sell at 98.2% of the last list price; 36% sold above list. They had a median $535 per square foot, a median year built of 1986 and a median strata fee of $471 a month. 4 condos sold in Eagle Ridge, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Eagle Ridge?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 10 condos and townhomes listed in Eagle Ridge. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Eagle Ridge a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Eagle Ridge had a sales ratio of 30%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Eagle Ridge from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 10 condos and townhomes sold in Eagle Ridge over those 5 months, out of 596 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What attached stock does Eagle Ridge actually have?
faq.a: Two City-documented complexes on Lansdowne Drive. Eagle Ridge Court at 1170 Lansdowne Drive is a strata conversion approved through the City's Subdivision Committee process in 1980, applied for by Cressey Development Corporation, and the townhouse project at 1135 Lansdowne Drive is a 16-unit project the City's Design Committee reviewed in 1988.

faq.q: Why does Eagle Ridge Court's paperwork mention tenants?
faq.a: Because it started as a rental building. The July 3, 1980 Subdivision Committee minutes record the strata title conversion application for 1170 Lansdowne Street, the undertaking that existing tenants would not be ejected to ease sale of the units, and a recommended waiver of the 3.5% vacancy guideline. A buyer should expect conversion-era disclosure in the strata documents and should read the depreciation report with that history in mind.

faq.q: Is Eagle Ridge Hospital in Coquitlam?
faq.a: No — it is in Port Moody. Fraser Health lists Eagle Ridge Hospital at 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, which is the hospital at the west end of this Coquitlam neighbourhood's main street. For a Lansdowne Drive townhouse buyer, the practical point is that the closest hospital named by the health authority sits across the municipal border, not inside Coquitlam.

faq.q: Which schools are beside these complexes?
faq.a: Three schools on one corridor. School District No. Catchment is still by permanent home address in the SD43 School Locator — a 1135 or 1170 Lansdowne address must be run individually, not assumed from the walk.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Eagle Ridge sell for?
faq.a: 14 townhomes sold in Eagle Ridge between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $873,250.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Eagle Ridge?
faq.a: The median was 16 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 98.2% of the last list price (36% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
